title: Hello SME! Generating Fast Matrix Multiplication Kernels Using the Scalable Matrix Extension
problem: Scalable Matrix Extension (SME) on Apple M4 offers matrix acceleration potential, but its throughput characteristics and memory bandwidth constraints for matrix register operations are not well documented. Designing code generators to produce optimized SME matrix multiplication kernels is challenging without this understanding.
motivation: Modern CPUs with matrix acceleration units like SME can deliver significant performance improvements for compute-intensive workloads, but require specialized code generation strategies to effectively exploit their capabilities.
method: The authors measure Apple M4's Scalable Matrix Extension (SME, a hardware feature for accelerating matrix math) by testing how fast it performs floating-point and fixed-point operations and measuring memory bandwidth when using matrix registers (fast on-chip storage). They discover that two-step loading and storing—rather than single transfers—achieves optimal bandwidth. They then build a just-in-time code generator that automatically creates optimized matrix multiplication code for Apple M4.
key_novelty: A code generator that automatically produces optimized matrix multiplication kernels for Apple M4 by measuring how its matrix extension hardware actually performs.
contributions: Comprehensive microbenchmark analysis of Apple M4's SME throughput and bandwidth characteristics
Discovery that optimal matrix register bandwidth requires two-step load/store operations
Just-in-time code generator for SME-optimized small matrix multiplications
Demonstration of superior performance compared to vendor-optimized BLAS implementations

metrics.speedup: outperforms vendor-optimized BLAS in most configurations

limitations: Not discussed in abstract; applicability to other architectures or larger matrices beyond small matrix multiplications is unclear.
primary_theme: Matrix acceleration code generation for ARM SME
